report.source_text: The peripheral blood analysis showed a lymphocyte population of about 38.6% with no apparent abnormal antigen expression ( Figure 1 ). The B-cells were approximately 10% of the lymphocytes and appeared polyclonal. There was however a small population (about 2.4% of all the lymphocytes) with a slightly higher side scatter that showed brighter CD19, and CD20. By collecting about 1,000,000 cells in all events, it showed monoclonal kappa light chain, while the remainder of the B cells were polyclonal.

report.source_text: Review of the bone marrow morphology demonstrated normocellular marrow with B-cell infiltrate representing 30-40% of the marrow cellularity that were predominantly medium sized mature forms with oval-shaped nuclei and appreciable cytoplasm with cytoplasmic projections. clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old male presented with mild thrombocytopenia (platelets 120K/μL) detected on CBC with otherwise normal WBC, RBC, and hemoglobin. Flow cytometry on admission revealed a small monoclonal B-cell population (2.4% of lymphocytes) with kappa light chain restriction and brighter CD19/CD20 expression. Three weeks later, bone marrow biopsy and aspirate demonstrated a normocellular marrow with 30-40% B-cell infiltrate consisting of medium-sized mature forms with characteristic oval nuclei and cytoplasmic projections. Comprehensive immunophenotyping showed the abnormal B-cells were positive for CD19, CD20, CD22, HLA-DR, FMC7, CD25, CD103, kappa monoclonal, Annexin A1, DBA44, BCL1, BCL2, TRAP, and BRAF V600E, while negative for CD5, CD10, LEF1, and BCL6. On follow-up, the patient developed splenomegaly on ultrasound and complained of fatigue, consistent with disease progression.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The 30-40% bone marrow infiltrate with characteristic morphology, comprehensive immunophenotype including CD25, CD103, TRAP positivity, and BRAF V600E mutation are diagnostic of clonal disease, specifically hairy cell leukemia, not a benign process
The immunophenotype is negative for CD5, which is typically positive in CLL. The presence of CD25, CD103, TRAP, and BRAF V600E is characteristic of HCL, not CLL
The bone marrow morphology with characteristic cytoplasmic projections, TRAP positivity, and BRAF V600E mutation are specific for hairy cell leukemia, not marginal zone lymphoma
